what: The verdicts the third project (counter, plan node X7) is expected to get. Written and committed BEFORE the pipeline was run on its rules. Compared with out/graph.json by `python3 counter/check_expected.py` (run from clausal/, after ./run.sh).

Rule.counter_rules.rejected_bump_unchang.why: true: bump returns false before it writes; proved for every counter and every amount by a hand-written proof of the generated obligation

Rule.counter_rules.bump_always_accepted.why: false: a bump that would pass 100 is rejected (for example a counter at 0 bumped by 101); refuted in the kernel at an input, and that input must fail on the compiled Rust too

Rule.counter_rules.bump_resets.why: no book the project lists has a word for `resets`: the line is not a composition of pieces, no statement

fn:lean:counter.Counter.bump.why: input coverage is computed from proved universal SCENARIOS of the old glossary; the counter has Rule lines only, and no trivial-model entry, so no suite adequacy verdict either

no_other_verdict: no other verdict of out/graph.json may name the counter
